substitutes: No long line? A regular six-foot leash works; you stay close to the dog.
title: The Punch Card Trail
clue: Out is a stroll. Back is an exam with four questions.
reveal: On your way out you quietly seed a loop with four hidden scents. On the way back, your dog works each landmark with their nose while you tick a punch card. It is orienteering for a dog who would rather follow a smell than a map.
objective: Seed four landmarks on an out-and-back walk, let your dog find each cloth on the return, and finish with a sniff scatter.
instructions: Pick a loop you can walk in 25 to 40 minutes from your door: a park path, a green strip or a green strip. Choose four landmarks you can say in two words (green trash can, big oak, bench, gate) and type them in a phone note. That note is your punch card.

Make the controls: tear four cloths bigger than your dog's head (a hand-towel corner each) from an old towel and rub each against your dog's treats for a minute. Keep them in a zip bag. Put the treats in your pocket and use a harness with a six-foot leash or a long line.

Out leg: a normal sniffing walk. At each landmark, tuck a cloth under or beside it while your dog nose-browses nearby. Skip anything near a road, water edge, steep slope or a spot other dogs use. No treats yet.

Return leg: at the first landmark, stop, drop the leash slack and say 'find'. Let your dog work a circle of about ten feet around it. When the nose lands on the cloth, say 'yes', treat from your pocket, tick the card and pocket the cloth. Do not point.

If your dog is stuck: stand still for a count of ten, then walk a slow half circle around the landmark so the air moves. Still nothing? Step toward the cloth yourself and let your dog find it with you beside it. A find with help is still a find.

Hard stop: if a dog, bike or squirrel takes your dog's full attention (hard staring, hauling, whining), shorten the line, move away to a quiet patch and finish as a plain walk. Never reel your dog in by force or chase.

Finish chute: at the last landmark, check the patch first, then scatter a small handful of treats into long grass or leaves and sit while your dog forages. Offer water, count your four cloths and walk home on a loose leash.
twist: The walk out is the setup and the walk back is the exam: your dog finds each hidden cloth by nose while you tick a punch card.
variations: Easier: only two controls, and put the cloths on the edge of the path itself.
No-park version: use four lamp posts or gates on a quiet street, on a short leash only, with the same steps. Long line: park or green strip only.
Wet or hot day, at home: pick four furniture landmarks inside, hide the cloths in different rooms and run the same card.
Harder: put cloths higher on a low bench or farther from the path, and add one control the dog never saw you place.
completion: It counts when the card has at least one tick, or when you have walked the return leg, even if your dog finds none and prefers to sniff the hedge.
photoIdea: Your dog at the final landmark with nose in the grass, and the phone punch card in the corner of the frame.
memoryPrompt: Which landmark fooled your dog, and which one did they find first?
dietNotes: Rewards come from your pocket after a find; no food is left outside. Check treat labels for xylitol and ask your vet about diet limits.
safety: Let your dog sniff the cloth, not chew it: lift it when the nose lands. Skip it if your dog mouths fabric.
Harness, not collar, on a long line; never wrap it round your hand. Collect every cloth; check the patch first.
Check leash rules, keep clear of wildlife, and skip hot or icy ground.
